title: Logical Cohesion via Routing Control Flags
pattern: A single function executes entirely different operations depending on a control flag (enum or boolean) passed in as an argument.
why_bad: The operations are only bound together by the control flow inside the method, which artificially inflates complexity. It forces callers to supply irrelevant arguments (e.g., passing `None` to a `Read` call) and couples unrelated task changes.
detection: A function takes a control flag parameter that immediately drives a top-level `match` or `if/else` block partition, where each branch performs a distinct, non-overlapping workflow.
counterexample: Factory patterns or dispatchers where the sole, explicitly documented purpose of the struct is polymorphic routing.
source: *Steve McConnell - Code Complete, Chapter 7, Section "Aim for Strong Cohesion" (Logical Cohesion)*
